CalCs (short for "Calendar Complications") is a watchOS-only app that provides various calendar-related complications.

--- Important Notes ---
The functionality embedded in the main body of the app includes only event list and monthly calendar views.
Other functions are carried out via complications or Smart Stack.
To display a 1-month calendar in complications, Series 7 or later models (excluding SE) that support Modular Duo watch face are required.
(Even on models that do not support Modular Duo watch face, it is possible to display a 2-week or 3-week calendar in complications, or display a 1-month calendar in Smart Stack.)
-----------------------

Key Features:
●Supports various complications such as date display, event display, and month calendar display
・Date Display:
Displays the current date in various formats.

・Next Event Display:
Displays next event synced with iPhone, including all-day event based on user preference.
*In circular complications, only the 1st 3 characters of event titles are displayed.

・Next 3 Events Display:
Displays the next 3 synced events from iPhone, optionally including all-day events.

・Month Calendar Display:
Displays the current month's calendar, optionally starting with Monday.
It's also possible to display the next event together.
Offers 4 types: 2 weeks showing (this week and next week), 3 weeks showing (last week, this week, and next week), and the 1st half of the month and the 2nd half of the month.
Placing 1st half and 2nd half types in Modular Duo or Smart Stack allows viewing a full month calendar.

●The main body of the app displays a list of events and monthly calendars
In the app launched by tapping complications, it displays event lists synced with iPhone and monthly calendars.

Event list view allows:
・Scroll to view events for the previous month, current month, and next 3 months.
・Long tap to scroll to current events.
・Swipe right to switch to monthly calendars view.
*Event addition, editing, and deletion functions are not currently implemented.

Monthly calendars view allows:
・Scroll to view calendars for the previous month, current month, and next 3 months.
・Double tap to switch between starting on Sunday or Monday.
・Long tap to scroll to the current month.
・Swipe left to return to event list view.

●Minimal Settings
Due to the small screen of Apple Watch, settings are limited to selecting displayed calendars only.



*Notes:
・Corner complications, circular complications, and large rectangular complications operate on Apple Watch Series 4 and later. Therefore, CalCs does not guarantee operation on Series 3 and earlier models.

・Due to watchOS complications update restrictions, there may be delays in updates after changes like adding or editing events on iPhone.

・It may take considerable time from placing complications for them to appear.

・If complications do not update, launching CalCs via complication tap might trigger an update. Please try this if needed.

・If complications still don't update, force quit CalCs and restart it. To force quit:
1. Long press the side button with CalCs open.
2. When the emergency call/power off screen appears, long press the digital crown.

If full access to the calendar is not granted the 1st time it is launched, CalCs will not ask for access permission again. In that case, you will need to clear the permission once from the iPhone and re-allow it from CalCs.
1. Open "Calendars" under "Privacy and Security" in the iPhone Settings app.
2. Change the access to the calendar in CalCs to "None" once, and then select "Add Events Only".
3. Tap "Allow full access" when you are asked to allow full access when opening CalCs.

・Downloading CalCs from the App Store on iPhone may lead to sync issues preventing it from appearing on Apple Watch. As watchOS-only apps cannot be re-downloaded from iPhone's App Store app, please search and re-download "CalCs" from the App Store on Apple Watch if this occurs.

The most important functions for iPhone and iPad:

- Sensor data can be recorded at up to 100Hz (depending on the iOS device version and sensor type).
- Sensor data can be streamed in server or client mode using TCP or UDP. Depending on the network speed and the server or client configuration used, this is possible with up to 100Hz.
- Via HTTP(S) GET/POST request, sensor data in JSON format (POST) or form-url encoded (POST and GET) can be transmitted to a REST API with up to 20Hz.
- With the SensorLog Remote Client/Server function, an iPad or iPhone can connect as a SensorLog Remote Client to an iPhone or iPad, which takes on the role of SensorLog Remote Server. The client's sensor data can be visualized on the server, and the server can control the clients (start/stop logging, start/stop sending data).
- Logging can be started and stopped using Siri and shortcuts.
- SensorLog supports Core ML models created with Apple's Create ML app. Log data with SensorLog, train a model with the data in Create ML, load exported models in SensorLog and log the model prediction. Supported Create ML models are: Activity Classifier, Tabular Regressor and Tabular Classifier.
- If you have an Apple Watch, HealthKit data such as heart rate, energy used, sleep and movement data can be exported on the watch as a csv or json file and then transferred to your iPhone.
